summary: proxy-chain is a programmable HTTP/HTTPS proxy server for Node.js (think Squid) developed by Apify. It enables dynamic proxy chaining, authentication, SOCKS4/5 support, HTTPS CONNECT tunneling, custom HTTP responses, and traffic statistics. The primary use case is making headless Chrome/Puppeteer work with authenticated upstream proxies since Chrome doesn't support proxy URLs with passwords. The library exposes a Server class with a prepareRequestFunction callback that determines per-request whether to authenticate, chain to an upstream proxy (HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS), return a custom response, or route CONNECT tunnels to a custom server. It also provides helper functions: anonymizeProxy() to convert authenticated proxies to local anonymous ones, createTunnel() for TCP tunneling through HTTP proxies, and listenConnectAnonymizedProxy() to intercept CONNECT response headers. Version 3.0.0 (May 2026) modernized to ESM-only, Node 20.11+, and added Bun support.

findings.description:
- HTTP/HTTPS proxy server with configurable port/host
- Dynamic per-request authentication via prepareRequestFunction callback
- Upstream proxy chaining (HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4, SOCKS4a, SOCKS5, SOCKS5h)
- HTTPS CONNECT tunneling for arbitrary protocols (HTTPS, FTP, etc.)
- SOCKS protocol support with authentication
- Custom HTTP responses without contacting target (HTTP only)
- Custom CONNECT server routing
- Connection pooling via custom http/https Agents
- Traffic statistics per connection (bytes sent/received)
- TLS/SSL support with secure defaults (TLS 1.2+)
- anonymizeProxy() - converts authenticated proxy to local anonymous proxy
- createTunnel()/closeTunnel() - TCP tunneling through HTTP proxy
- listenConnectAnonymizedProxy() - intercept CONNECT response headers
- Detailed error codes (590-599) for upstream failures
- RequestError class for custom error responses
- Graceful shutdown with connection draining

apiSurface:
Main exports from 'proxy-chain':
- Server class: new Server(options) with listen(), close(), getConnectionStats(), getConnectionIds(), closeConnection(), closeConnections()
- Events: 'requestFailed', 'connectionClosed', 'tlsError', 'tunnelConnectResponded', 'tunnelConnectFailed'
- anonymizeProxy(url | options): Promise<string> - returns local anonymous proxy URL
- closeAnonymizedProxy(anonymizedProxyUrl, closeConnections): Promise<boolean>
- createTunnel(proxyUrl, targetHost, options): Promise<string> - returns local endpoint
- closeTunnel(serverPath, closeConnections): Promise<boolean>
- listenConnectAnonymizedProxy(anonymizedProxyUrl, callback): boolean
- redactUrl(url, passwordReplacement): string
- RequestError class for custom error responses
- Types: ServerOptions, PrepareRequestFunction, PrepareRequestFunctionResult, ConnectionStats
integrationPoints:
- Playwright/Puppeteer: Use anonymizeProxy() to convert authenticated proxy URLs to localhost proxies that browsers can use (--proxy-server=localhost:xxxx)
- Queue integration: Server can run as long-lived proxy pool; prepareRequestFunction can implement per-request proxy rotation from a queue
- Search/matching: Custom responses can intercept and mock responses; CONNECT header interception enables proxy fingerprinting
- Pipeline: Create multiple Server instances on different ports for proxy pools; use connection stats for monitoring; graceful shutdown fits ETL job boundaries
- TLS: HTTPS server type with custom certs for MITM-style interception if needed
strengthsForVeridian:
- Solves the exact problem of authenticated proxies with headless browsers (Puppeteer/Playwright)
- Corporate-backed (Apify), production-proven via Crawlee adoption
- Modern async API, TypeScript-first, well-tested (unit + e2e + docker)
- Flexible per-request routing via prepareRequestFunction - can implement proxy rotation, geo-targeting, auth per domain
- Low-level control: custom responses, CONNECT interception, byte-level stats
- SOCKS support broadens proxy provider compatibility
- Active maintenance (v3.0 May 2026, Bun support)
weaknessesForVeridian:
- Node.js only - not usable from Python/other runtimes directly
- Runs as separate proxy server process (not in-process) - adds operational complexity
- No built-in proxy pool management, rotation, health checks - must build on top
- Single-threaded Node.js event loop may bottleneck high-throughput scraping
- ESM-only may require build step changes for some toolchains
- No built-in metrics export (Prometheus, etc.) - only programmatic getConnectionStats()
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
